# Q05 quest handlers (eltnen, poeta, oriel): deviations and generated files

## P6-Q ascension route, lane route-gen (2026-09-29)

The first generated quest handlers of the port, for the retail Ascension route (owner, 2026-09-29: "Try to prioritize things that would get
Ascension running sooner"). Generated by `cpp/tools/gen/questgen` (phase6-questgen-prototype.md), compiled into `aion_gs_handlers_quest_q05`,
checked by `tools/parity` and driven through the real engine by the golden trace harness of this chunk's test directory. Uncommitted in the
lane's worktree for the integrator. Q09.md (ishalgen) and the "Generated dispatches" section of Q06.md (ascension) are the other two parts;
the generator changes, tests and the gate impact below are shared by all three.

### Generated files

`game-server/handlers/aion/gameserver/handlers/quest/poeta/`, from `game-server/data/handlers/quest/poeta/` (9 files, tier A except `_1205`):
`_1001TheKerubThreat`, `_1003IllegalLogging`, `_1004NeutralizingOdium`, `_1005BarringtheGate`, `_1107TheLostAxe`, `_1111InsomniaMedicine`,
`_1122DeliveringPernossRobe`, `_1123WheresTutty`, `_1205ANewSkill` (tier B: `PlayerClass.getStartingClass`).

Regenerate (from `cpp/`): `python -m tools.gen.questgen --dry-run --emit <dir outside the repo> --only poeta/<file>.java ...`, then copy
`<dir>/aion/gameserver/handlers/quest/poeta/*.cpp` into the tree. `tools/gen/tests/test_questgen_tree.py` regenerates every tree file that
carries the generator's banner and fails on any byte of difference, so the tree is the generator's output with **no hand edit**.

**Held back (gate impact, below):** `_1000Prologue` and `_1100KaliosCall` transliterate (the drift test checks they still do) and passed all
their golden cases, but they are not in the tree. Both register `onEnterWorld` and start their quest at a character's first enter world, as
Java does; that turns gs.scenario.m5a, m5b and m5b2 red. They land as soon as the gates' owners decide (the same regenerate command).
**Consequence until then:** every mission handler in the tree (1001, 1003, 1004, 1005 here; 2001, 2003, 2005, 2006 in Q09) is unlocked only
by `defaultOnQuestCompletedEvent` or `defaultOnLevelChangedEvent` with 1100 (2100) among its pre-quests, and nothing in the tree starts 1100 or
2100 (they have no XML script either), so on a fresh character the landed missions register but can never start; 1005 also needs 1002, which
another lane ports by hand. The owner's gate decision is the only thing between these files and a playable Poeta/Ishalgen mission chain.

Not generated here: `_1002RequestoftheElim` and `_1114TheNymphsGown` (questgen refuses them: `_1002` an anonymous `Runnable` and
`new SM_ASCENSION_MORPH`, `_1114` a lambda); other lanes port them by hand.

**Java bugs kept and marked** (phase6-inventory.md §11, U3; questgen's `KNOWN_JAVA_BUGS` writes the `// java-bug kept` line, the golden
harness pins the behaviour): `_1004NeutralizingOdium.java:68` `targetId == 700030 && var == 1 || var == 4` is `(… && var == 1) || var == 4`,
so at var 4 any target, none included, takes the cauldron branch (USE_OBJECT sets var 5, removes 182200005 and returns false: oracle cases
onDialogEvent#2 and #21); `_1111InsomniaMedicine.java:60, :62, :72, :81` dereference `qs` without a null check in the 203061 branch, so a
player without 1111 gets a NullPointerException there, which `QuestEngine.onDialog` catches (C++: `Ptr` throws `NullPointerException`,
`QuestEngine::onDialog` catches `std::exception`), ending that npc's talk loop (XML quests 1106 and 1108 at 203061 are skipped for him).

### Generator changes (shared with Q09 and Q06)

| Change | Where | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| The banner says the file is generated and compiled: `// Generated by cpp/tools/gen/questgen from <java>.` and `// Compiled into its Q chunk's handler library (game-server/chunks.cmake). Do not edit: change the generator and regenerate.` (was `(prototype) ... Not compiled.`) | `tools/gen/questgen/emit.py` (`banner`, `BANNER_FIRST_LINE`) | All 929 of the 929 files the driver emits (of 1,035 Java handlers) change, in these two comment lines only: measured by emitting all of them with the old and the new banner and diffing (no other line differs) |

No compile fix was needed. The 36 route files built with no error and no warning under the project flags (`/W4`) in the unity build and file
by file (`AION_HANDLER_UNITY=OFF`, `TreatWarningAsError=true`). The emitter already writes the `AION_QUEST_HANDLER(Class, id);` marker last
in the namespace. `tools/parity` finds all 36 at parity with their Java (`parity.py tree`: 36 pairs, 0 with mismatches). Golden expectations
of the tool's own tests: none pinned the banner, so none changed.

### Tests

`game-server/tests/quest_handlers_golden/` (Q05's test directory, `aion_gs_handlers_quest_q05_tests`; chunks.cmake `TESTS quest_handlers_golden`):

- `GoldenQuestTraceTest.cpp`, `EveryCaseMatchesTheJavaTrace/Quest<id>` (one per generated handler): every case of
  `tools/oracle/expected/quest/<id>.json` (tools/oracle/questtrace, written from the Java) runs twice on the real engine from the same state
  (quester of the quest's race and minimum level with the parts a loaded player has, the case's QuestState, inventory, target npc and dialog
  action, the real static data rows of the quests, npcs and items the traces name): once through the generated handler's hook, once by
  replaying the Java trace's effects on the real helpers (AbstractQuestHandler through a PlainHandler, QuestService, the QuestState setters).
  The SM_DIALOG_WINDOW, SM_QUEST_ACTION and SM_PLAY_MOVIE packets (bytes), the opcode sequence of all packets, every QuestState afterwards, the
  inventory and the return value (or the NullPointerException) must be equal. A case whose guards assume a helper result gets the first setup
  whose replay reproduces it (own race and minimum level; plus finished prerequisites; plus the collect items held; level 1; the other race;
  quest list full). Every run reseeds the thread's `Rnd` with one seed on the fixture's `ManualClock` (phase6-inventory.md §7.6 item 3).
- **Overlays** (the route-gen review, 2026-09-29): the oracle's given holds only what the hook reads, so a helper the path calls often did
  nothing in either run, and a deleted reward step, kill step or chain trigger passed. Each case now also runs with inputs its given leaves
  out, which the hook therefore does not read on that path, but its helpers do: a dialog action when the path reads none (the reward page,
  the finish, SET_SUCCEED, accept, refuse), the items a `removeQuestItem` names and the quest's collect items, each npc of a
  `defaultOnKillEvent` list as the target when the path reads none, var slot 0 at a step helper's step when the path leaves it free (the
  oracle's new `free`), and the pre-quests of the chain helpers finished with the quest's first permitted class, at its level and one below.
  The oracle's new `atHigh` entries (the same path with a ranged input at its high end: `var < 6` at 5, `itemCount >= 3` at 2) run as cases of
  their own, and the test checks that every case and high end of the document ran. A case with effects that no run makes observable (no
  packet, no QuestState or inventory change) must be listed in `knownVacuous` with its reason: 27 are, each a helper called in a state the
  path itself fixes (sendQuestEndDialog at a status or dialog action it ignores, sendQuestStartDialog with USE_OBJECT, startQuest assumed
  false).
- `HandTracesOfTheClassSkillQuests`: 1205 and 2132 (A New Skill), whose hooks the oracle refuses, get a trace written by hand from the Java in
  the oracle's format (per starting class: the level hook's start, REWARD, var and reward group; the class npc's page and end dialog; another
  class's npc) and run through the same harness: 27 cases each.
- `TheHarnessFailsDeliberatelyWrongHandlers`: a copy of `_1111InsomniaMedicine` with one flip at a time (page, var, reward group, item count,
  status, return value) must fail 1111's cases through the comparison that sees it; unflipped it must pass them all.
- `EveryRunStartsFromTheSameRandomStateOnTheManualClock`: a handler that draws its page from `Rnd` sends the same page in two runs, and the
  scheduler's clock is the fixture's ManualClock.
- `RegistrationTraceMatchesJavaRegister` (phase6-inventory.md §7.6 item 2): each handler registered alone, behind a spy that runs its
  `register_()`. The quest id sits in each QuestNpc list as often as the Java `register()` adds it and in no other registered npc's list; the
  engine events (quest completed, level changed, enter world, enter zone, quest item use, can act) reach the handler exactly for the Java
  registrations, including the can-act registration QuestNpc adds for a `quest_use_item` npc (QuestNpc.java:59-95), and
  `isRegisteredQuestItem` answers for the registered item. The order of registrations to different lists inside one `register_()` is not
  observable in engine state; the drift test pins it.
- `EveryExpectedDocumentHasAGeneratedHandlerAndEveryHandlerADocument`: both directions (a missing trace fails, it is not skipped).

Result on the tree as delivered: **727 of 727** (694 cases of 32 documents plus 33 high ends; 1,724 compared runs with the overlays, 3 overlay
runs no setup reproduces), 54 of 54 hand cases, 37 of 37 tests. Before the review, the first run on the committed traces had 733 cases with
all 36 handlers: 724 passed, 0 failed, 9 not reproducible. The 9 were paths the oracle wrote although Java can never take them:
`giveQuestItem(env, id, 1)` "-> false" (1004 #17 #31, 1111 #18 #21, 1122 #3, 2106 #10 #18, 2135 #3; AbstractQuestHandler.java:626-641) and
`collectItemCheck(env, true)` "-> true" with no QuestState (1111 #2, QuestService.java:557-561). **Oracle fix** (`extract.py`
`dead_assumption`, test `test_helper_results_java_cannot_return_are_dead_paths`): such paths are dropped (the first slice has 506 cases).
`knownNotReproducible` is empty. With the four held-back files compiled in for a measurement (emitted to a scratch directory, the table
and `GOLDEN_HELD_BACK` edited, then restored by sha256): their 30 cases pass under the overlays (1000: 8, 1100: 7, 2000: 8, 2100: 7) and the
registration trace passes with all 36, enter-world routing included; their two vacuous cases (1100 #4, 2100 #5: sendQuestStartDialog with
USE_OBJECT) are listed in `knownVacuous` already, so the files land by the regenerate command and a table edit only.

The generated ishalgen and ascension files are compiled into this executable by `#include` (`GoldenIshalgenHandlers.cpp`,
`GoldenAscensionHandlers.cpp`), because a handler target's tests link only their own library; P5-05's tests do the same for two quest npc AIs
(the P5-05 LEASE row of chunks.cmake). Manifest request p6q-m01 (docs/porting/header-requests.md) records it, and the comment on Q05's row of
chunks.cmake names the two included chunks.

Python: `tools/gen/tests/test_questgen_tree.py` (the banner; the 32 route files are in the tree with it; every bannered tree file regenerates
byte for byte; the 4 held-back files transliterate and stay out of the tree; the two Java bugs are kept and marked);
`tools/oracle/tests/test_quest_trace.py` (`RouteSliceTest`: the route slice and hand-derived 1913 cases;
`test_ranged_inputs_are_traced_at_their_high_end`; `test_unguarded_var_reads_are_free`); `test_questgen_p6t.py` and `RealSliceTest` read
`SLICE_TIER_A` (the 20-quest slice).

Mutation proof (`AION_QGEN_MUT`; sources saved and their sha256 checked after the restore, rebuilt, stale PDBs dropped, no mutant string in any
source, object, library, executable or PDB). Before the review: a flipped page (1001 #3), item count (1001 #7), var (1913 #4), status (1913
#7) and registration npc (2001) failed; `oracle-page`, `oracle-dead` and `banner` failed their tests. After it, the review's survivors, all
killed now: `q1001_end` (the REWARD branch returns false: dialog overlay), `q2001_krew` and `q2001_kend` (kill step deleted, end var 7:
target overlay), `q1913_done` (the dispatch's chain trigger deleted) and `q1001_chain`, `q1003_lvl` (1100 read as 1101: chain overlay),
`q1111_rmid`, `q2135_rm` (wrong or no item removed: item overlay), `q2001_chk` (check page 1695: var overlay), `q29071_endnpc` (any npc
rewards: dialog overlay), `q1001_kill`, `q1003_rng`, `q2114_rng`, `q1001_cnt` (boundaries moved by one: `atHigh`), `q1003_inc`, `q2114_inc`
(`var + 1` read as 2: `atHigh`), `q2132_rg`, `q2132_page`, `q2132_status` (hand traces), `q2122_item`, `q1001_noreg` (quest item and
quest-completed registration: registration trace); harness mutants `h_page`, `h_state`, `h_self` (negative control), `h_seed` (Rnd test),
`h_nooverlay` (24 quests fail: their cases turn vacuous), `h_missing` (a missing trace is a failure in both tests), `h_highoff` (the variant
count); Python `o_high`, `o_free`, `g_bug` fail their new tests and the committed-trace or drift test. With the switch unset, all pass.

### Gate impact

Every generated handler registers in every gate (the registry has no per-profile switch, and none of these checks
`CustomConfig.ENABLE_SIMPLE_2NDCLASS`). Measured on gs.scenario.m5a, m5b and m5b2 in this worktree:

| Handlers in the server | m5a | m5b | m5b2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| none (HEAD) | pass | pass | pass |
| all 36 | **fail** | **fail** | **fail** |
| 34 (without 1000, 2000) | **fail** | **fail** | **fail** |
| 32 (without 1000, 2000, 1100, 2100: the tree as delivered) | pass | pass | pass |

With the 32, gs.scenario.m5b3 and m5c pass too.

With the enter-world quests in, the first enter world of the gates' level-1 characters sends `SM_QUEST_ACTION` at packet #2 where the recorded
sequence has `SM_NEARBY_QUESTS`, and the quest list is no longer empty (`M5aScenarioTest.cpp:865`, `:1623`; `M5bScenarioTest.cpp:537`;
`M5b2ScenarioTest.cpp:446`); the later cases do not run and the end-of-run reports fail. This is Java's behaviour (`_1000Prologue.java:22`, `:26-36`,
`_1100KaliosCall.java:26`, `:56-61` and their Ishalgen twins start the quest at enter world), so the fix belongs to the gates, not to the handlers.
Under the owner's rule (U1/U7: a phase-6 lane that turns a phase-5 gate red is reverted, not fixed forward) the four are held back and **no
gate expectation was changed**. Decision needed: update the three gates' first-enter-world expectations (or seed their characters with 1000 /
2000 complete and 1100 / 2100 present), then land the four files.

### Left

- The four enter-world handlers (1000, 1100 here; 2000, 2100 in Q09) wait for the gates' decision above.
- `tools/porting/lint_concurrency.py` is run on `game-server/src` (the gate `gs.lint.concurrency` and this lane's checks): 0 findings. Run on
  the handler tree it reports L2 for three generated files whose constant Java `int[]` field the emitter writes as `static constexpr
  std::array` (`_1003IllegalLogging::mob_ids`, `_2001ThinkingAhead::mobs`, `_2122AshesToAshes::npcs`; fieldmap.json expects
  `Ref<Array<int32_t>>`). The emitter's mapping is phase6-inventory.md §7.1's (the field is never written, which questgen checks); the lint
  needs a rule for generated constant arrays, or the emitter a change, before the handler tree joins the lint.
- 1100's and 2100's enter-world and level hooks are not traced (WorldMapType); 1205 and 2132 are traced by hand, not by the oracle.
- An unguarded read of anything but a var slot is not varied yet (the oracle's `free` lists var slots only); the 27 listed vacuous cases
  are the helpers no sound overlay reaches.
